claims.sentence: The MHRA warned of disruption to blood ketone testing after Nova Biomedical recalled StatStrip ketone test strip lots and paused distribution.
claims.evidence: Title: risk of disruption to blood ketone testing due to quality-control failures and supply interruption; recall initiated and distribution of affected lots paused.

claims.sentence: The MHRA issued a Device Safety Information notice on 9 October 2026 about Nova Biomedical StatStrip ketone test strips.
Nova Biomedical has recalled specified lots after repeated quality-control failures and paused distribution of those lots.
claims.evidence: 'specified lots ... associated with repeated QC failures'; 'initiated a recall'; 'paused distribution of the affected lots'.

claims.sentence: The company says it cannot replenish UK stock for roughly four weeks.
claims.evidence: 'unable to replenish UK stock levels for approximately 4 weeks'.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says losing timely ketone testing could delay recognition and treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis.
claims.evidence: Retrieved text: risk of 'delayed recognition or exclusion of DKA'. 'Treatment' (and 'escalation') not confirmed; the first search did not return the DKA wording at all.
claims.newSentence: The MHRA says disruption to ketone testing risks delayed recognition or exclusion of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).

claims.sentence: The MHRA says Nova Biomedical has recalled specified lots of StatStrip ketone test strips after repeated quality-control failures and has paused distribution of those lots.
Any further lots that fail quality control are to be withdrawn, which could steadily reduce the strips available for clinical use.
claims.evidence: 'any further lots found to fail QC testing should also be withdrawn from use'; 'may result in a progressive reduction in the availability of ketone test strips'.

claims.sentence: The company has said it cannot replenish UK stock for about four weeks.
The MHRA warns that losing timely ketone testing can delay recognition, escalation and treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), and that this could contribute to serious harm or death.
claims.evidence: The second search explicitly found no 'serious harm or death' wording; 'escalation and treatment' not confirmed either. Only 'delayed recognition or exclusion of DKA' is retrieved. Do not publish the harm/death claim unless read on the page.
claims.newSentence: The MHRA warns that disruption to ketone testing risks delayed recognition or exclusion of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).

claims.sentence: DKA is a serious complication of diabetes.
claims.evidence: Not in retrieved text; plain textbook fact.

claims.sentence: Where supply is limited, the MHRA advises clinicians to prioritise testing for patients at greatest risk, including those with suspected or established DKA, children, and acutely unwell people with type 1 diabetes.
claims.evidence: 'prioritise blood ketone testing for patients at greatest clinical risk ... suspected or established DKA, paediatric patients, acutely unwell patients with type 1 diabetes, patients requiring serial ketone measurements'. Clinician-directed.

claims.sentence: A separate National Patient Safety Alert on the supply disruption was issued on 13 October 2026.
claims.evidence: Retrieved: 'national supply disruption alert' NatPSA/2026/007/NSDR listed as issued 13-Oct-2026 on the MHRA Central Alerting System (cas.mhra.gov.uk). The expansion 'National Patient Safety Alert' is not in the text; the page that carried the line is uncertain (search listed several CAS pages).
claims.newSentence: A separate national supply disruption alert (NatPSA/2026/007/NSDR) was issued on 13 October 2026, according to the MHRA Central Alerting System listing.

claims.sentence: The site's type 1 diabetes page gives background on the condition.
claims.evidence: Site-navigation sentence; not from retrieved text.

notes: Both dates confirmed: 9 October (DSI) and 13 October (NatPSA/NSDR, CAS listing only). 'Serious harm or death' and 'escalation and treatment' must go.
